input.question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?
input.ground_truth: Because you remember the best, eventful memories in more detail. You tend to block out all the normal things like changing you socks or taking a shit that day. Similar to when you zone out in the shower trying to think if you've just washed your hair or not. You do those things everyday and block them out of memory.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy box. When you look at your toy box from far away, it looks really fun and full of cool toys. But when you open the box and look at each toy up close, some toys might be broken or not as fun as you remember.

Our memories are like that toy box. When we think about things that happened long ago, we mostly remember the happy and fun parts, like looking at the toy box from far away. But if we remember everything—good and not so good—it might not seem as nice as we thought.

So, things from the past can seem better in our memory because we forget the not-so-fun parts and just remember the happy ones!
